senses.definition: A line of rulers from the same family, or the stretch of time when that family rules.
senses.example: The Tang dynasty ruled China for almost three hundred years.

senses.definition: A number of lands or peoples governed from one main center of power.
senses.example: The empire grew as it took control of nearby cities.

senses.definition: A group of travelers who make part of a trip together, often carrying goods.
senses.example: The caravan carried salt across the desert.

senses.definition: A tall building with wide steps or layers, built in some ancient cities of the Middle East.
senses.example: The ziggurat at Ur rose high above many other buildings.

senses.definition: An animal bone or turtle shell used to ask questions about the future in ancient China.
senses.example: A writer cut signs into an oracle bone.

senses.definition: Baked clay, often orange or reddish brown, used for pots, tiles, and figures.
senses.example: The artist shaped a terracotta figure from soft clay.

senses.definition: An upright carved slab or pillar, often put up to remember a person or event.
senses.example: The carved stele stood near an old grave.

senses.definition: A journey to a place that is special to a person’s religion or beliefs.
senses.example: Mansa Musa’s pilgrimage took him across North Africa.

senses.definition: A flat, level area cut into a slope or built above the ground.
senses.example: The builders made a broad terrace for the palace.

senses.definition: A carved, drawn, or printed sign that represents something, such as a sound, word, or number.
senses.example: The Maya writer used a glyph for a day in the calendar.

senses.definition: A city and the land around it that have their own government.
senses.example: Tikal was a Maya city-state.

senses.definition: A raised garden made from mud, plants, and other materials in shallow water, with canals around it.
senses.example: The farmer reached her chinampa by boat.

senses.definition: A set of cords with knots that people in the Andes used to keep information.
senses.example: The quipu held a record of quantities.

senses.definition: A large round or oval performance space with rows of seats around an open middle.
senses.example: The crowd filled the seats in the amphitheater.

senses.definition: A long, narrow boat that people used in the Viking Age, with a sail and places for oars.
senses.example: The crew rowed the longship away from the shore.

senses.definition: A curved structure that spans an opening and helps hold up what is above it.
senses.example: The stone arch carried the weight of the wall over the doorway.

senses.definition: A waterway made by people to carry boats or to move water.
senses.example: A small boat traveled along a canal between gardens.

senses.definition: A round roof or ceiling that curves upward like part of a ball.
senses.example: Sunlight streamed in through windows under the dome.

senses.definition: A place controlled by another country, often after people from that country settle there.
senses.example: Massachusetts was once a British colony.

senses.definition: To approve a written agreement by following its official rules.
senses.example: Several states had to ratify the new Constitution.

senses.definition: To officially put an end to a rule or practice.
senses.example: The Thirteenth Amendment said the country must abolish slavery.

senses.definition: Forced separation of groups of people, such as rules that keep children of different races in separate schools.
senses.example: Families went to court to challenge segregation in public schools.

senses.definition: An organized refusal to buy, use, or take part in something in order to protest.
senses.example: The boycott lasted more than a year as residents refused to ride the buses.

senses.definition: A person who comes to live in another country.
senses.example: The museum keeps records of immigrants who sailed into New York Harbor.

senses.definition: An official statement meant to be heard or read by the public.
senses.example: The president issued a proclamation to announce the decision.

senses.definition: A plan for a new law, written so lawmakers can talk about it and vote on it.
senses.example: The state lawmakers discussed a bill about public libraries.

senses.definition: A paper or another tool that lists choices for an election and lets a voter mark a choice.
senses.example: Ana watched her mother fill in a ballot at the voting place.

senses.definition: A group chosen to hear information and make a decision in a court case.
senses.example: The jury listened to the witnesses before making its decision.

senses.definition: The decision a jury or judge gives at the end of a trial.
senses.example: The judge read the verdict aloud after everyone returned.

senses.definition: A legal process through which someone becomes a citizen of a country after birth.
senses.example: At the end of naturalization, the new citizens took an oath.

senses.definition: A group of written signs. Each sign generally stands for one spoken syllable rather than a single sound.
senses.example: Sequoyah made a syllabary for writing Cherokee.

senses.definition: A word that people speaking one language take from another language and start using.
senses.example: A word may become a loanword when cooks teach other people the name of a dish.

senses.definition: Lettering written with care as a form of art.
senses.example: The invitation was decorated with blue calligraphy.

senses.definition: An outer arch that carries a push from the upper part of a building out to a strong support on the ground.
senses.example: A flying buttress supported the wall beside a tall window.

senses.definition: A tower with one or more levels and specially shaped roofs, found in parts of Asia and often connected with Buddhism.
senses.example: The garden path led past a stone pagoda.

senses.definition: Earth mixed with water and sometimes plant material, then formed into bricks or walls and allowed to dry.
senses.example: The thick adobe walls blocked the heat in the afternoon.
